Test-fixture cleanup and performance work are complete. Transactional database and invoice helpers were corrected; invoice tests pass 46/46, payment tests 63/63, customer tests 31 with 2 skipped, subscription tests 52 with 3 skipped, and report tests 28/28. The full Python suite passes 318 tests with 4 skipped in roughly 15 seconds, down from 42 seconds. Shared factories resolved setup failures, including the factory-bound payment-method fixture. Production billing paths remain unchanged. Search isolation/rebuild, UTF-8 CSV export, storage behavior, and billing typing have been validated. Avoid introducing retries or richer idempotency behavior at this stage.

The remaining issue is an intermittent invoice-sync integration failure: one of eight tests expects HTTP 202 but occasionally receives 409. Repetition with `--count=20` produced one failure, confirming a concurrency race when workers submit the same invoice with the same idempotency key. Database inspection found key `test-inv-1042` stuck in `processing`, despite the original request completing successfully. Next, inspect API idempotency middleware and determine whether concurrent duplicate keys should wait/replay the completed result or return 409; add a narrowly scoped test and avoid broad retry changes.

Before handoff, verify invoice credit/refund total semantics and the `Returning Any` warning in the final diff. The Go rename from `get_user_record` to `fetch_account` is complete but still needs tests. Operational follow-up: settlement reconciliation, end-to-end payment verification, and staging worker-pool validation at five workers; higher counts need `#staging-ops` approval.
